questions._flag: Official key kept as printed, but recorded as a disagreement for a human. Electron and proton beams travelling the same way constitute ANTIPARALLEL conventional currents, so the magnetic force between them is repulsive - which is the reasoning option (b) rewards. The charges are however OPPOSITE, so the Coulomb force is attractive, and at non-relativistic beam speeds it exceeds the magnetic force by roughly \((c/v)^2\), making the net force attractive. The item is answerable only if the magnetic interaction is read as the one being asked about. The SAME question, with the SAME key (b), is printed as Q5 of sibling set 55/2/1, so this is CBSE's settled position across the series, not a one-paper slip.
